entries:
ܕܪܳܓܳܐ rt. ↗ ܕܪܓ. m. a step, taking a step.
p. 98

ܕܪܳܟ݂ܳܐ, ܕܪܳܟ݂ܬ݂ܳܐ rt. ↗ ܕܪܟ. f. the treading out or thrashing of corn
ܬܰܘܪܳܐ ܕܕܳܪܶܟ݂ the ox that treadeth out the corn
p. 98

ܕܪܰܡ only Pael pass. part. ܡܕܰܪܰܡ, ܡܕܰܪܡܳܐ, ܡܕܰܪܡܬ݂ܳܐ cunning, crafty, tricky.
Derivatives ↗ ܕܪܽܘܡܳܐ, ↗ ܡܕܰܪܡܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ
p. 98

ܕܪܰܡܰܐ pl. ܕܪܰܡܰܛܰܐ δρᾶμα, a fable, drama.
p. 98

ܕܪܽܘܡܽܘܢ pl. ܕܪܽܘܡܽܘܢܶܣ f. δρόμων, a sort of light vessel.
p. 98

ܕܪܽܘܡܽܘܢܳܪܶܐ or ܕܪܽܘܡܽܘܢܳܪܝܶܐ m. pl. dromonarii, rowers of a dromon, boatmen.
p. 98

ܕܰܪܡܣܽܘܩ rarely ܕܰܡܣܩܽܘܣ pr. n. Damascus.
p. 98

ܕܰܪܡܣܽܘܩܳܝܳܐ, ܝܬ݂ܳܐ from the above, damascene.
p. 98

ܕܰܪܰܥ denom. verb Pael conj. from ↗ ܕܪܳܥܳܐ; to steer, rule; to take any one by the arm.
p. 98

ܕܪܳܥܳܐ pl. ܕܪ̈ܳܥܺܝܢ, ܕܪ̈ܳܥܶܐ m. the arm, the shoulder; a sleeve.
p. 98

ܕܰܪܳܫܳܐ pl. ܕܰܪ̈ܳܫܶܐ rt. ↗ ܕܪܫ. m. a wrestler, athlete, warrior, combatant.
p. 98

ܕܰܪܳܫܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ rt. ↗ ܕܪܫ. f. prowess; conflict; a contest.
p. 98

ܕܪܰܫ fut. ܢܶܕܪܽܘܫ, inf. ܡܶܕܪܰܫ, act. part. ܕܳܪܶܫ, ܕܳܪܫܳܐ, pass. part. ܕܪܺܝܫ, ܕܪܺܝܫܳܐ, ܕܪܺܝܫܬ݂ܳܐ (root-meaning to thresh or tread out) to tread, find out or prepare a path, with ܐܽܘܪܚܳܐ or ܫܒ݂ܺܝܠܳܐ. Metaph. to practise, train, instruct, esp. with ܢܰܦ̮ܫܳܐ; with ܥܰܡ to dispute, debate. Pass. part. trodden, worn; common, trite
ܠܳܐ ܕܪܺܝܫ untrodden, pathless
Pa. ܕܰܪܶܫ to practise, train, instruct
ܒܐܽܘܪܚܳܐ ܕܚܰܝܶܐ in the way of life
Pass. part. ܡܕܰܪܰܫ, ܡܕܰܪܫܳܐ, ܡܕܰܪܫܬ݂ܳܐ practised, trained, learned
ܡܕܰܪ̈ܫܺܝܢ ܒܡܰܟ݂ܬ݂ܒ݂ܳܢܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ—ܒܟ݂ܬ݂ܳܒ݂ܶܐ learned men
Ethpa. ܐܶܬ݂ܕܰܪܰܫ to be open, trodden of a road; to be disputed, debated; to be exercised, trained, instructed, with ܩܪܳܒ݂ܳܐ to be expert in war
ܒܕܽܘܒܳܪܳܐ ܕܢܙܺܝܪܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ in the ascetic life
Derivatives ↗ ܕܪܽܘܫܳܐ, ↗ ܕܽܘܪܫܳܐ, ↗ ܕܽܘܪܫܳܢܳܐ, ↗ ܕܪܳܫܳܐ, ↗ ܕܪܳܫܬ݂ܳܐ, ↗ ܡܕܰܪܫܳܐ, ↗ ܡܕܰܪܫܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ, ↗ ܡܕܰܪܫܳܢܳܐ, ↗ ܡܶܬ݂ܕܰܪܫܳܢܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ
p. 98

ܕܽܘܪܳܫ, ܕܽܘܪܳܫܳܐ rt. ↗ ܕܪܫ. m. treading or pounding; metaph. with ܥܰܡ or ܠܘܳܬ݂ a disputation, controversy, controversial treatise
ܒܶܝܬ݂ ܕܽܘܪܳܫܳܐ pl. ܒܳܬܰܝ̈ ܕܽܘܪܳܫܳܐ a gymnasium, school
p. 98

ܕܽܘܪܫܳܢܬ݂ܳܐ f. some herb, perh. cyclamen or hellebore.
p. 98

ܕܰܫ 3 m. s. pret. of ↗ ܕܘܫ.
p. 98

ܕܰܫܶܢ denom. verb Pael conj. from ↗ ܕܶܫܢܳܐ; to give, grant.
Ethpa. ܐܶܬ݂ܕܰܫܰܢ to be given.
p. 98

ܕܶܫܢܳܐ E-Syr. ܕܰܫܢܳܐ pl. ܕܶܫ̈ܢܶܐ Pers. m. a gift.
p. 98

ܕܳܬ݂ܳܐ Heb. and Chald. an edict, judgement, law.
p. 98

ܗ the fifth letter of the alphabet. The cardinal number 5
ܕܗ ordinal the fifth
p. 98

ܗ̄ abbreviation for
a) ܗܳܢܰܘ that is, i.e.
b) Hallelujah, ܗ̄ ܘܗ̄ or ܗ̄ ܘܗ̄ܠ Hallelujah, Hallelujah.
p. 98

ܗܳܐ interjection demonstrative or emphatic Lo! Behold! often used in expressions of time already, now, these
ܗܳܐ ܬܡܳܢܰܥܶܣܪܶܐ ܫܢܺܝܢ—ܗܳܐ ܥܶܣܪܺܝܢ ܫܢܺܝܢ Lo these eighteen years, twenty years
in adverbial expressions of time here, this
ܡܶܢ ܗܳܐ ܗܳܫܳܐ from this very time
ܡܶܢ ܗܳܐ ܘܰܠܗܰܠ from this time onwards, henceforth
ܡܶܢ ܗܳܐ ܡܶܟܺܝܠ henceforward
With ܕ
ܕܗܳܐ for behold, because, already
ܠܳܐ ܗܳܐ interrog.—not? is it not so?
p. 98–99

ܗܰܒ݂, ܗܰܒ݂ܘ, ܗܰܒ݂ܝ, ܗܰܒ݂ܶܝܢ imperative of verb ↗ ܝܗܒ, give, put &c.; interj. of encouragement or exhortation, come.
p. 99

ܗܰܒܶܒ denom. verb Pael conj. from ↗ ܗܰܒܳܒܳܐ; to bloom, blossom; metaph. to flourish, glitter, to be showy; act. part. ܡܗܰܒܶܒ, pass. part. ܡܗܰܒܰܒ florid, adorned, splendid, foaming as new wine
ܓܶܘܢܶܗ ܕܐܰܦܰܘ̈ܗܝ ܕܡܗܰܒܰܒ ܗܘܳܐ his complexion which had been florid
ܒܛܰܪ̈ܦܶܐ ܡܗܰܒܰܒ ܗܘܳܐ wreathed or garlanded with leaves
p. 99

ܗܰܒܳܒܳܐ pl. ܗܰܒ̈ܳܒܺܝܢ, ܗܰܒ̈ܳܒܶܐ a flower, blossom
ܗܰܒ̈ܳܒܶܐ ܕܓܰܘ̈ܢܶܐ flowers of various colours
ܗܰܒܳܒܳܐ ܕܢܚܳܫܳܐ verdigris
ܗܰܒܳܒܳܐ ܕܚܰܠܝܳܐ saltpetre
Derivatives ↗ ܗܰܒܶܒ verb, ↗ ܗܰܒܳܒܬ݂ܳܐ, ↗ ܡܗܰܒܒܳܢܳܐܺܝܬ݂, ↗ ܡܗܰܒܒܳܢܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ
Cognates ↗ ܐܶܒܳܐ, ↗ ܐܒܳܒܳܐ
p. 99

ܗܒܶܠ, ܗܒ݂ܳܠܳܐ m. vanity, emptiness
ܗܒܶܠ ܗܒ݂ܳܠܺܝܢ vanity of vanities
ܚܰܝܰܝ̈ ܗܒ݂ܳܠܳܟ݂ thy vain or empty life
Derivatives ↗ ܗܰܒܠܳܢܳܐ, ↗ ܗܰܒܠܳܢܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ
p. 99

ܗܶܒ݂ܠܳܐ pl. ܗܶܒ݂̈ܠܶܐ m. a herd, swineherd.
p. 99

ܗܰܒ݂ܠܳܐ m. a rare form for ↗ ܗܶܒ݂ܠܬ݂ܳܐ; see below.
p. 99

ܗܰܒ݂ܠܳܢܳܝܳܐ, ܗܰܒ݂ܠܳܢܳܝܬ݂ܳܐ pl. m. ܗܰܒ݂ܠܳܢܳܝ̈ܶܐ f. ܗܰܒ݂ܠܳܢܳܝ̈ܳܬ݂ܳܐ adj. from ↗ ܗܒܠ; vain, empty, pl. m. followers of vanity.
p. 99

ܗܶܒ݂ܠܬ݂ܳܐ or ܗܰܒ݂ܠܬ݂ܳܐ f. a herd, drove, line esp. of camels.
Cognate ↗ ܐܰܒ݂ܠܬ݂ܳܐ
p. 99

ܗܰܒܳܒܬ݂ܳܐ from ↗ ܗܰܒܳܒܳܐ. f. a bloom, blossom.
p. 99

ܗܓ݂ܳܐ imper. ܗܓ݂ܝ to meditate with ܒ of the subject.
Ethpa. ܐܶܬ݂ܗܰܓܺܝ to meditate;
a) to plan or scheme with ܕ of the intention, with ܥܰܠ or ܠܘܳܬ݂ against
ܨܶܒ݂ܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ ܐܶܬ݂ܗܰܓܺܝܘ they planned this affair
ܡܳܪܽܘܕܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ ܐܶܬ݂ܗܰܓܺܝ ܠܽܘܩܒ݂ܠܶܗ he plotted rebellion against him
b) to read syllable by syllable, study, brood over; gram. to vocalize.
Derivatives ↗ ܗܶܓܝܳܐ, ↗ ܗܶܓܝܳܢܳܐ, ↗ ܗܶܓܳܐ, ↗ ܗܽܘܓܳܐ, ↗ ܡܗܰܓܝܳܢܳܐ, ↗ ܡܗܰܓܝܳܢܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ, ↗ ܡܶܬ݂ܗܰܓܝܳܢܳܐ
p. 99

ܗܓܓ not used in Pe.; root-meaning to dream, see visions in sleep.
Pa. ܗܰܓܶܓ to imagine, fancy.
Ethpa. ܐܶܬ݂ܗܰܓܰܓ to fancy, imagine, conceive mentally, devise
ܫܰܪܺܝ ܠܡܶܬ݂ܗܰܓܳܓܽܘ ܦܰܢܛܰܣܺܝ̈ܣ ܡܛܰܢ̈ܦܳܬ݂ܳܐ he began to conceive foul fancies
Derivatives the seven following words, ↗ ܗܽܘܓܳܓܳܐ, ↗ ܡܶܬ݂ܗܰܓܓܳܢܳܐ, and ↗ ܡܶܬ݂ܗܰܓܓܳܢܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ.
p. 99

ܗܰܓܳܓܳܐ pl. ܗܰܓ̈ܳܓܶܐ rt. ↗ ܗܓܓ. m. an imagination, illusion, idea
ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܕܗܰܓ̈ܳܓܶܐ ܘܕܚܶܠܡ̈ܶܐ this world of illusions and dreams
ܗܰܓ̈ܳܓܶܐ ܕܡܶܢ ܟܬ݂ܳܒ݂ܶܐ ideas from books
p. 99

ܗܽܘܓܳܓܳܐ rt. ↗ ܗܓܓ. m. a phantom, apparition, appearance, illusion
ܠܳܐ ܗܘܳܐ ܗܽܘܓܳܓܳܐ the ram sacrificed instead of Isaac was no phantom
p. 99

ܗܓܳܓܳܐ pl. ܗܓ̈ܳܓܶܐ rt. ↗ ܗܓܓ. m. imagination, the imaginative faculty, the second of the five mental senses.
p. 99

ܗܽܘܓܳܓܳܐܺܝܬ݂ rt. ↗ ܗܓܓ. adv. in vain semblance, spuriously.
p. 99

ܗܽܘܓܳܓܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ pl. ܗܽܘܓܳܓܘܳܬ݂ܳܐ rt. ↗ ܗܓܓ. f. a phantom, illusion, imagination; a vain fancy, show or pomp; the heresy of the Phantastiasts.
p. 99

ܗܽܘܓܳܓܳܝܳܐ, ܗܽܘܓܳܓܳܝܬ݂ܳܐ rt. ↗ ܗܓܓ. adj. fantastic, fanciful; a Phantastiast.
p. 99

ܗܽܘܓܡܳܢܳܐ rt. ↗ ܗܓܡ. m. ruin, destruction in the active sense, cf. ↗ ܗܓܺܝܡܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ.
p. 99

ܗܶܓܝܳܐ rt. ↗ ܗܓܐ. m. meditation; severe suffering.
p. 99

ܗܓܺܝܡܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ rt. ↗ ܗܓܡ. f. ruin, destruction in the passive sense.
p. 99

ܗܶܓܝܳܢܳܐ pl. ܗܶܓܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ rt. ↗ ܗܓܐ. m. meditation, study, subject of study; reading by syllables as a beginner, a syllable
ܫܰܪܺܝܢܰܢ ܒܰܟ݂ܬ݂ܳܒ݂ܶܐ ܗܶܓܝܳܢܳܐ we began to learn reading
ܚܰܕ ܗܶܓܝܳܢܳܐ monosyllabic
ܕܰܬ݂ܠܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܗܶܓܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ trisyllabic
ܡܫܽܘܚܬ݂ܳܐ ܕܬ݂ܡܳܢܝܳܐ ܗܶܓܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ octosyllabic metre
ܩܳܠܳܐ ܕܗܶܓܝܳܢܳܐ an articulate sound
ܒܗܽܘܢ ܗܶܓܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ in these very words
p. 99

ܗܓܰܡ fut. ܢܶܗܓܽܘܡ, act. part. ܗܳܓܶܡ, ܗܳܓܡܳܐ, pass. part. ܗܓܺܝܡ to ruin, destroy, overthrow, break down, hew down.
Ethpe. ܐܶܬ݂ܗܓܶܡ to be ruined.
Pa. ܗܰܓܶܡ to break down, ruin utterly.
Derivatives ↗ ܗܽܘܓܡܳܢܳܐ, ↗ ܗܓܺܝܡܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ
p. 99

ܗܶܓܡܽܘܢܳܐ, ܗܶܓܡܽܘܢ or ܗܶܓܡܘܢ pl. ܗܶܓܡܽܘܢ̈ܶܐ m. ἡγεμών, a prefect, procurator, governor; hegoumenos or prior of a monastery.
p. 99

ܗܶܓܳܝܳܐ pl. ܗܶܓܳܝ̈ܶܐ rt. ↗ ܗܓܐ. m. reading, the art of reading; a syllable.
p. 99

ܗܳܓܳܪ pr. n. Hagar
ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܗܳܓܳܪ or ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܗܳܓܰܪ Arabs, Saracens
Derivatives the three following, ↗ ܐܰܗܓܰܪ, ↗ ܡܗܰܓܪܳܝܳܐ and ↗ ܡܗܰܓܪܳܝܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ.
p. 99

ܐܰܗܓܰܪ denom. verb Aphel conj. from the above; to become a Mohammedan, apostatize to Islam
ܡܰܗܓܪ̈ܶܐ perverts to Islam
Ethpa. ܐܶܬ݂ܗܰܓܰܪ the same.
p. 100

ܗܳܕ (rare), ܗܳܕܶܐ fem. this
ܗܳܕܶܐ ܗ̱ܝ this is
see ↗ ܗܳܢܳܐ.
p. 100

ܗܕܳܐ fut. ܢܶܗܕܶܐ, part. ܗܳܕܶܐ, rare in Pe. to lead, direct.
Pa. ܗܰܕܺܝ to lead, direct, with ܠ
ܟܽܠܗܶܝܢ ܕܦܰܩܶܕ ܥܰܡ ܘܰܡܗܰܕܺܐ everything that he hath commanded and directed us to do
Ethpa. ܐܶܬ݂ܗܰܕܺܝ to be led, guided; with ܐܺܝܕܳܐ by the hand; to follow, with ܒ or ܒܳܬ݂ܰܪ
ܒܝ ܢܶܬ݂ܗܰܕܶܐ let him follow my example
Derivatives ↗ ܗܰܕܳܝܳܐ, ↗ ܗܰܕܳܝܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ, ↗ ܗܰܕܝܳܢܳܐ, ↗ ܗܽܘܕܳܝܳܐ, ↗ ܡܗܰܕܝܳܢܳܐ, ↗ ܡܗܰܕܝܳܢܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ, ↗ ܡܶܬ݂ܗܰܕܝܳܢܳܐ, ↗ ܡܶܬ݂ܗܰܕܝܳܢܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ
p. 100

ܗܰܕܪܐܶܝܠ a corruption of the Heb. harel = mount of God; metaph. the altar.
p. 100

ܗܰܕܳܝܳܐ, ܗܰܕܳܝܬ݂ܳܐ pl. m. ܗܰܕ̈ܳܝܶܐ f. ܗܰܕ̈ܳܝܳܬ݂ܳܐ rt. ↗ ܗܕܐ. a leader, guide, teacher.
p. 100

ܗܶܕܝܽܘܛ, ܗܶܕܝܽܘܛܳܐ m. ܗܶܕܝܽܘܛܺܝܬ݂ܳܐ f. pl. m. ܗܶܕܝܽܘܛܺܝܢ, ܗܶܕܝܽܘܛܶܐ f. ܗܶܕܝܽܘܛܝܳܬ݂ܳܐ ἰδιώτης, simple, untaught, ignorant
ܗܶܕܝܽܘܛܳܐ ܒܩܶܪ̈ܝܳܢܶܐ ignorant of reading
ܗܶܕܝܽܘܛܳܐ ܒܝܽܘܠܦܳܢܳܐ unlearned
stupid, plebeian; pl. common people.
p. 100

ܗܶܕܝܽܘܛܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ f. ἰδιωτεία, ignorance, lack of knowledge, want of experience.
p. 100

ܗܰܕܳܝܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ rt. ↗ ܗܕܐ. f. leading, direction; way, manner.
p. 100

ܗܰܕܝܳܢܳܐ pl. ܗܰܕܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ rt. ↗ ܗܕܐ. m. a leader, guide, teacher.
p. 100

ܗܕܺܝܪܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ rt. ↗ ܗܕܪ. f. comeliness, excellence; honour
ܗܕܺܝܪܽܘܬ݂ ܚܰܝܶܐ an honourable life
p. 100

ܗܰܕܳܡ, ܗܰܕܳܡܳܐ pl. ܗܰܕ̈ܳܡܺܝܢ, ܗܰܕ̈ܳܡܶܐ m. a limb, member, part of the body
ܗܰܕ̈ܳܡܶܐ ܐܺܝܕ̈ܳܝܶܐ the hands and feet
ܗܰܕ̈ܳܡܶܐ ܓܰܘ̈ܳܝܶܐ the internal organs
ܗܰܕ̈ܳܡܶܐ ܐܰܘܟܺܝܬ݂ ܕܟܝܳܢܳܝ̈ܶܐ, ܡܫܰܡܫܳܢ̈ܶܐ &c. the genital organs
ܦܣܳܩ ܗܰܕ̈ܳܡܶܐ mutilation
ܗܰܕܳܡ ܗܰܕܳܡ limb by limb, piecemeal
Metaph. a part of a discourse, a part of speech, a word or syllable.
Derivative the following— ↗ ܗܰܕܶܡ
